modules.module_title: Review the status of previous day's work

pcs.pc_description: Review the agenda for the day and brief the team on objectives, priorities, and important updates.
Communicate any special tasks, challenges, or deadlines and update the team members on operational targets and key metrics.
Assess the previous day's reports with supervisors, including inspection and output reports.
Identify pending works and approve pending orders of the previous day.
Resolve issues about pending activities or escalate them to senior management or an external consultant/ technician.
Review performance and utilisation of budgeted resources, making amendments as required.
Ensure the department meets its daily performance targets.
Confirm that all necessary resources (materials, equipment, personnel) are available and aligned with the day's tasks.
Analyse any operational challenges from the previous day, such as bottlenecks or delays, and ensure they are resolved.

modules.module_title: Forecast and budget resources for operations

pcs.pc_description: Analyse trend patterns and make suitable assumptions for forecasting.
Prepare forecasts and accordingly plan and budget for workforce and other resources.
Set up consensus meetings with peers and seniors and get their approval on the forecast and budgets.
Prepare weekly and monthly work plans as per the forecast and budget.
Make amendments to budgeted resources based on daily performance reviews.

modules.module_title: Approve work plans and allocate tasks

pcs.pc_description: Identify priority tasks and inform supervisors and executives.
Approve and share the weekly work plan with supervisors, allocating resources per the plan.
Review and approve any ad-hoc request for alternate or additional resources.
Approve daily work plans prepared by supervisors and examine staff turnover issues.
Take immediate action to address discrepancies, such as allocating additional resources or providing guidance to staff.
Coordinate with other departments and external resources to escalate and expedite stuck cases.
Actively promote knowledge and resource sharing with peers and across functions.
Administer & optimise administration processes and procedures.
Prepare reports, MIS and other artefacts as necessitated by the senior management.
Identify the avenues for driving cost efficiency and productivity.
Actively manage department budget.
Focus on new revenue opportunities while strengthening and sustaining current revenue opportunities.
Coordinate with clients and keep them updated on delays, pendency, etc.
Analyse the work of executives and supervisors to check for errors.
Review reports to monitor operational performance.
Guide the team in using the latest technology, ERP, and available IT infrastructure.
Address any equipment breakdowns, staffing shortages, or safety concerns.
Coordinate with relevant teams to troubleshoot and find quick solutions.

modules.module_title: Ensure compliance with legal and regulatory framework

pcs.pc_description: Monitor compliance with relevant local, country and international laws and processes regularly.
Monitor compliance concerning organisational policies and procedures.

modules.module_title: Manage material handling and inventory operations

pcs.pc_description: Ensure proper selection of material handling equipment (e.g., forklifts, conveyors, automated guided vehicles) and tools are available for transporting materials within the plant
Review material Requirement Plan (MRP) for weekly, monthly, and quarterly requirements in coordination with the materials department
Optimise Storage systems such as shelving, racking, or bins for easy access.
Implement Automated systems like robotic arms, conveyors, or automated storage and retrieval systems (ASRS) to improve speed, accuracy, and efficiency

Establish appropriate inventory control techniques such as Just-In-Time (JIT) to reduce excess stock or Economic Order Quantity (EOQ) to balance inventory levels and demand while reducing holding costs
Ensure grouping of materials or components based on size, weight, or demand frequency for faster retrieval and better space utilisation
Analyse budget vis-v-vis actual procurement
Raise indent to the materials department for required items
Set automatic reorder points based on demand patterns to ensure that the necessary materials and components are always available without overstocking
Optimise the warehouse or storage area layout for efficient material handling, ensuring that frequently used items are easily accessible and high-demand materials are placed in optimal locations
Review the plan for material handling & transport vehicles based on the day load for receipt and storage
Approve inbound receipts, deliveries, and gate passes and assist the accounts department in approving invoices
Inspect inbound vehicle reports regarding material damage, accidents, etc
Review the allocation of labour and resources for unloading materials and transfer of stocks to the right storage location
Check the inspection report for the inbound stock
Examine and approve the supervisor's request for storage locations
Approve transfer orders in the Material Management System (MMS) to manage stock between multiple storage locations
Ensure that KPIs such as material availability, inventory turnover rates, order fulfilment time, and downtime are met
Review processes and performance data regularly to identify inefficiencies and implement improvements (e.g., lean manufacturing, Six Sigma)

modules.module_title: Receive despatch orders and manage delivery

Coordinate with the production department for in-plant material requirement
Coordinate with sales/dispatch department during material/finished goods/items movement for dispatch
Acknowledge the list of quantities for dispatch after assessing the physical quantity for material present in the warehouse vis-a-vis the requirement
Approve transfer orders, dispatch orders and material issue approvals in MMS
Review material dispatch orders and allocate labour and MHEs for transfer of the material to the desired department/location
Conduct periodic wall-to-wall inventory checks and update the ERP

pcs.pc_description: Oversee the return of materials from customers, suppliers, or field operations, ensuring that returns are processed efficiently.
Implement clear procedures for returns, including proper documentation (e.g., return merchandise authorisations, inspection reports) and tracking of returned items.
Supervise the inspection and assessment of returned goods or materials to determine whether they can be reused, refurbished, resold, or need to be scrapped.
Classify returned items based on condition (e.g., damaged, defective, excess stock) and decide the appropriate action.
Ensure that items that can be restocked (such as undamaged, unopened, or lightly used materials) are properly inspected, repacked, and returned to the inventory.
Work closely with the customer service or sales teams to ensure that returns or exchanges are processed promptly, supporting customer satisfaction and retention.
Provide insights and recommendations to optimise reverse logistics operations.
Analyse data on returns to identify root causes (e.g., defects, customer dissatisfaction) and work with other departments to improve product quality or reduce return rates.
Stay updated on relevant laws and best practices to mitigate the risk of penalties or environmental harm.
Evaluate the return rate and reasons for returns to identify trends.
Implement strategies like better product descriptions, quality control, or pre-purchase education to reduce the number of returns.
Use historical data and trends to anticipate returns and adjust inventory levels accordingly, ensuring the inventory system can account for expected returns.

modules.module_title: Monitor Repair, Recycling and Refurbishment of returned goods

pcs.pc_description: Ensure that repairs are done promptly and cost-effectively for materials that can be repaired or refurbished by coordinating with repair teams or third-party vendors.
Ensure that repaired items are properly labelled, recorded, and reintroduced into the inventory.
Oversee the sorting and responsible disposal of materials that cannot be reused, ensuring compliance with environmental regulations for waste disposal.
Implement procedures for safely handling hazardous materials or products with limited life cycles (e.g., electronics or chemicals).
Analyse components of disposable goods or a product that is no longer sellable and harvest any usable components or parts that can be reused or resold.
Implement technology like barcode scanning, RFID, and real-time inventory tracking to streamline return and reverse logistics processes.

modules.module_title: Manage documentation and compliance of reverse logistics

pcs.pc_description: Utilise inventory management software or systems to track returned items and ensure accurate documentation of returns, repairs, and recycling processes.
Regularly check whether the inventory levels are updated to reflect the impact of returns, repairs, and disposals on stock levels.
Ensure compliance with industry standards, government regulations, and environmental laws related to product returns, repairs, and disposal.
Monitor and report on reverse logistics performance, including return rates, costs, and inventory impact.
Ensure clear documentation of restocked items is maintained to update the inventory system accurately.

Classify products into A, B, and C categories based on their sales volume and store high- demand (A) items near the picking area to reduce picking time.

Use historical data, sales trends, and market analysis to predict demand and adjust inventory levels accordingly.
Implement automatic reordering systems based on predefined thresholds to avoid stockouts while minimising excess inventory.
Assign specific tasks (e.g., receiving, picking, packing) to specialised workers to reduce time spent switching between tasks.
Implement demand-based labour scheduling to ensure the right number of workers are available during peak hours and reduce labour costs during off-peak hours.
Apply key performance indicators (KPIs) like picking accuracy, order cycle time, and inventory turnover to measure performance and identify areas for improvement.
Use algorithms or WMS systems to optimise the picking path and minimise travel time within the warehouse.
Implement software that helps optimise shipping routes, calculate optimal packaging sizes, and compare carrier rates to reduce transportation costs.
Organise products in the warehouse based on demand (ABC analysis), ensuring fast-moving items are easily accessible and slow-moving items are stored further away.
Implement a flexible slotting system that adjusts based on seasonal demand, sales trends, or inventory changes.
Optimise aisle width based on equipment (e.g., narrow aisles for forklifts, wider aisles for manual picking).
Use drive-in racking or high-bay shelving for low-demand or large-volume items.
Optimise the racking by maximising the vertical storage space, e.g., using Selective Pallet Racks, Push-Back Racks, or adding Mezzanine Floors.
Ensure cross-aisles connect different zones and reduce travel time.
Minimise backtracking or unnecessary movement by planning for a one-way flow of goods (receiving → storage → picking → packing → shipping).
Empower workers to suggest small, actionable changes to improve their work environment.
Conduct regular audits to assess warehouse performance, identify bottlenecks, and evaluate efficiency.
Track KPIs to gauge improvement using data-driven metrics.
Use tools like Pareto Analysis, Fishbone Diagrams, or 5 Whys to identify the root causes of inefficiencies or issues and take corrective action.
Compare your warehouse operations with industry best practices or competitors to identify areas where you can improve.
Train employees regularly on safety protocols, proper equipment handling, and emergency procedures to reduce accidents.
Continuously track performance and make data-driven decisions for further optimisation.
Create standard operating procedures (SOPs) to ensure consistency and improve efficiency across the warehouse.
Ensure continuous improvement efforts remain aligned with changing business needs and warehouse operations.
Choose energy-efficient lighting (sodium lights or high-frequency fluorescents) and recommend installing skylights, LEDs with sensors (intelligent occupancy sensors, motion sensors, heat maps), etc.
Use machinery and equipment like MHE that runs on electric or alternative clean energy.
